account:
Today I have been following my appointments and trying to distinguish witnessed events from town gossip. The unusual story concerns an alleged bridge or port change at the bakery. I heard townsfolk repeat that phrase, but I have seen no such change. My neighbour originally saw Builder give the baker a lantern and planks last night without knowing why. At tea today, the neighbour reported asking both parties: Builder said those were bakery supplies, not a bridge or port alteration, and Baker confirmed an eighty-loaf freight order—thirty-two delivered, eighteen collected, and the last thirty baked. I therefore think the supplies concern the baker's work, plausibly that order, though I have not personally verified their exact use or the bread movements. The rumour appears to have travelled farther than its supporting facts.

My scheduled grain inspection remains incomplete because I could not locate the miller. I asked the secretary to request a grain-stock report after office duties; I do not yet have a report or evidence of a grain problem. No council correspondence had arrived when I attended the afternoon letters appointment, and the secretary reported no further morning concerns. An approved eighteen-o'clock lighting addendum is secured with the office records, but I should consult those records rather than invent its details.

I am now at the stationer's stall on my way back for the 16:30 office appointment. The secretary requested a writable book to record the mill follow-up, so I intend to buy one here and bring it to the office.
